architecture_principles: the unit of decision is an experiment, not a formulation
value of information is computed by a deterministic scientific tool, not by an additional language model
every registered hypothesis carries an explicit pre-result prediction rule and an explicit falsification condition
a measurement that cannot separate any registered hypothesis scores zero discrimination, and that is a scientific result rather than a defect
weight sensitivity is reported as decision stability, never as model confidence
ties in the deterministic layer are reported as ties; the tool must not manufacture a preference it does not have
held-out result data are structurally removed before any payload is assembled
the mechanism question and the Agent framework are separate contributions and are reported separately

candidate_space.rationale: V4 deliberately reuses the byte-identical V3 lattice. Continuous-space optimization and any new wet-lab work are out of scope, so that the measured change between V3 and V4 is the decision object and the VOI layer, not the search space.

architecture.canonical_flow: planner(intent + failure mode) -> evidence/tool layer (including the deterministic VOI tool) -> proposer -> skeptic -> robustness adjudicator -> judge -> freeze
architecture.claim_boundary: V4.0.0 selects an experiment from pre-result evidence under an outcome-blind runtime. Its adjudication tests whether a registered hypothesis survives contact with the completed measurement. It is not a contemporaneous pre-experimental record and does not claim that the historical decision used this ranking.
architecture.name: PUR_NEW_VOI_GUIDED_EXPERIMENT_SELECTION_AGENT_V4
non_goals: adding a language model to compute value of information
adding Agent roles beyond planner, tools, proposer, skeptic, robustness adjudicator, judge and freeze
turning the study into a pure AI benchmark
weakening or replacing the rheological mechanism result
architecture.purpose: Outcome-blind scientific decision Agent that selects the next formulation x measurement EXPERIMENT by transparent value of information, rather than selecting a formulation candidate alone.

stages.role: identify the physical failure mode and the scientific question that the next experiment must answer, then request the evidence needed to judge experiments rather than formulations

execute read-only scientific tools, including the paper-derived state-aware rheology tool, external evidence retrieval, and the deterministic VOI tool that scores every formulation x measurement experiment card
propose the experiment with the highest scientific information value, stating the hypotheses it separates and what each possible outcome would establish
attack the proposed experiment on hypothesis coverage, confounding, interpretability of the primary observable, and whether the stated falsification criterion can actually be met by the measurement
adjudicate whether the proposed experiment survives the reported VOI weight sensitivity and the skeptic's strongest objection
commit to one experiment card, or abstain, and state the acceptance and falsification criteria that will adjudicate it
programmatically validate and freeze the experiment card with timestamps, model identifiers and cryptographic hashes of every input

architecture.supersedes_nothing: V4 is an independent architecture. configs/agent_v3.json, prompts/agent_v3_*.txt, src/pur_new/agent_v3.py and every frozen V3 run record remain unchanged and are not reinterpreted by V4.

voi_tool.explicitly_not: distance to any held-out formulation. No target coordinate enters any component, weight or tie-break.
voi_tool.formula: VOI = w_hyp * hypothesis_discrimination + w_unc * uncertainty_reduction + w_dec * decision_relevance + w_int * measurement_interpretability - w_ext * extrapolation_risk - w_proc * process_state_risk
voi_tool.name: score_experiment_cards
voi_tool.not_a_posterior: The local design contains six audited realizations and two thermal-hold trajectories. That does not support a calibrated Bayesian expected-information computation, so no posterior probability is fabricated. Weight sensitivity is reported instead.

decision_stability_sent_to_model.metric_is_not: model confidence; posterior probability; calibrated expected information
decision_stability_sent_to_model.tie_interpretation: The deterministic VOI layer is indifferent among the tied top experiments: they share an identical component vector. Tie-breaking is therefore a genuine task left to the Agent, and any selection inside this set cannot have been read off the VOI ranking.
decision_stability_sent_to_model.voi_formula: VOI = w_hyp * hypothesis_discrimination + w_unc * uncertainty_reduction + w_dec * decision_relevance + w_int * measurement_interpretability - w_ext * extrapolation_risk - w_proc * process_state_risk. Every component is normalized to [0, 1] by construction. This is a transparent normalized score with reported weight sensitivity, not a Bayesian posterior.

evidence_policy.description: For prospective/blind Agent evaluation. The Agent may see original-system measurements and external analogue evidence, but not the target validation formulation identity, its wet-lab outcome, or any outcome-derived labels.

judge_normalized.acceptance_criterion: Accept the dual-axis intervention as strong suppression over the reactive-core prediction if the mean SI_15_60 across at least two independent repeats is <3.80%, which is below half of the 7.61% linear-dilution prediction for reactive mass fraction 0.8000. This falsifies H-CORE at the formulation-level resolution and supports H-RESIN, while remaining compatible with H-DUAL.
judge_normalized.falsification_criterion: If the mean SI_15_60 across at least two independent repeats is >=7.61%, falsify H-RESIN and treat the result as consistent with H-CORE linear dilution. If the mean is <3.80%, falsify H-CORE; means from 3.80% through <7.61% are neither strong suppression nor clear linear-dilution falsification. No outcome from this dual-axis composition separates H-RESIN from H-DUAL.
judge_normalized.next_experiment_if_falsified: Run an acrylic-only 15% AC1920 composition with the same matched reactive-core fraction and M-HOLD-120 protocol, using controlled and recorded preparation history, verified modifier functionality, and recalculated NCO:OH stoichiometry where required; compare its mean SI_15_60 with the dual-axis result to test H-DUAL.
judge_normalized.primary_observable: SI_15_60 = (eta_60 - eta_15) / eta_15, percent, reported for each repeat and as the arithmetic mean across at least two independent repeats
judge_normalized.rationale: S1C41 combines 15% acrylic-like modifier with 5% minor tackifier-like modifier while retaining the E2 reactive-core proportions. M-HOLD-120 directly measures the established 120 C viscosity-growth failure mode and separates the 3.80% strong-suppression threshold from the 7.61% linear-dilution prediction by more than the declared 2.00% resolution. It is therefore the minimum-sufficient mitigation test, provided its result is interpreted as a coarse suppression test rather than as evidence distinguishing the two modifier hypotheses.
judge_normalized.stage_disagreements_resolved: I followed the Proposer and Robustness Adjudicator in selecting S1C41::M-HOLD-120 because it directly interrogates the least-resolved failure coordinate, is in the stable deterministic top set, and uses the smallest modifier burden among tied cards. I followed the Skeptic on interpretation: the experiment cannot distinguish H-RESIN from H-DUAL, cannot attribute suppression to either modifier axis, and requires explicit repeat aggregation and stoichiometry/functionality verification before strong formulation-level claims.

uncertainty_decomposition.evidence_coverage_uncertainty: The 15% acrylic and 5% minor-tackifier levels are within the supplied candidate evidence region, but external evidence is analogue evidence and does not establish the exact local response or modifier functionality.
uncertainty_decomposition.extrapolation_uncertainty: Low for the selected composition and hold window: the candidate lies within the supported modifier regions and the observable uses the measured 15-60 minute window. Uncertainty remains from applying the single-realization E1 reference and its 9.51% drift to the linear-dilution benchmark.
uncertainty_decomposition.measurement_uncertainty: The primary observable is directly read from eta_15 and eta_60 without model fitting; the declared matched-window discrimination threshold is 2.00 percentage points. At least two independent repeats are required, with the arithmetic mean prespecified.
uncertainty_decomposition.realization_state_uncertainty: Moderate-to-high because M-HOLD-120 does not control process state, six process fields are missing, and realization-specific viscosity displacement dominates the local variation. Preparation history and start-of-hold viscosity should be recorded.

planner.failure_mode: Time-dependent viscosity growth during prolonged residence at 120 C, with the magnitude of drift strongly dependent on formulation or material state.
planner.failure_mode_evidence: The original E5 formulation increased by 51.54% from 15 to 60 minutes and by 93.08% from 15 to 90 minutes at 120 C, compared with 9.51% and 16.85% respectively for E1.
planner.least_resolved_justification: The local data establish endpoint drift for E1 and E5, but provide no candidate-composition hold trajectories and only limited original hold sampling over 15 to 90 minutes. In contrast, temperature response has six measured temperatures across multiple E2 runs, while realized viscosity level has repeated temperature-sweep observations despite large spread.
measurement_requirements: Measure viscosity at 120 C at 15, 30, 45, and 60 minutes, with at least two independent preparation repeats, and report the matched-window SI_15_60 drift.
Use a formulation and comparison reference at the same reactive mass fraction so the observed drift can be compared with the E1_drift multiplied by the reactive mass fraction.
Include modifier-axis conditions that distinguish acrylic-like addition alone from acrylic-like addition combined with a nonzero minor tackifier-like fraction.
Record the full time trajectory rather than only an endpoint, and preserve the realized viscosity level at the start of the hold so drift is not confounded with an unmeasured state displacement.
planner.scientific_question: At matched reactive mass fraction and matched 120 C hold window, does modifier addition suppress viscosity drift substantially below the reactive-core linear-dilution prediction, and is suppression obtained by the acrylic-like axis alone or only when the minor tackifier-like axis is also active?

hypotheses_not_separated: H-RESIN versus H-DUAL: both predict low drift for this dual-axis composition; an acrylic-only hold is required to distinguish them.

outcome_interpretation.if_acceptance_criterion_met: If SI_15_60 remains below 3.80% across at least two repeats, drift is below half the 7.61% linear-dilution prediction. This supports H-RESIN over H-CORE, while remaining compatible with either H-RESIN or H-DUAL.
outcome_interpretation.if_falsification_criterion_met: If SI_15_60 is at or above 7.61%, H-RESIN is falsified and the result supports the reactive-core linear-dilution prediction of H-CORE. It would not distinguish H-RESIN from H-DUAL if the result is merely non-low rather than clearly aligned with the linear prediction.
outcome_interpretation.if_intermediate: A result between 3.80% and 7.61% does not meet the registered strong-suppression criterion and is not clearly linear within the stated resolution; it indicates partial or ambiguous suppression and requires follow-up, especially an acrylic-only hold to test H-DUAL.

ranked_alternatives.why_lower_value: It is deterministically tied but uses more acrylic modifier, increasing total intervention burden without improving direct observability or hypothesis-pair discrimination.
It is deterministically tied but uses 20% acrylic, a larger departure from the reactive core than necessary for the same CORE-versus-resin discrimination.
It is deterministically tied but adds still more acrylic loading without additional hypothesis separation.
It is deterministically tied but has the largest acrylic burden in the tied set and therefore is not the minimum sufficient intervention.
Its 7.5% minor-tackifier level lies outside the repeatedly documented 4.8-6.4% cluster, producing nonzero extrapolation risk while offering the same hypothesis separation.

proposer.reasoning: The 120 C matched-window hold directly measures the least-resolved failure coordinate and separates the linear-dilution core prediction from strong resin suppression using thresholds that exceed the 2.00% discrimination resolution. S1C41 covers both independently supported modifier axes, retains the E2 reactive-core proportions, and minimizes modifier burden among genuinely tied top cards. Its direct observable is not model-fitted, and its outcome explicitly tests both the favored suppression interpretation and its registered falsification.
proposer.tie_break_justification: S1C41 uses the smallest acrylic loading in the tied set, 15%, together with 5% minor tackifier. Both levels are inside externally supported regions, and 5% lies in the repeatedly documented minor-resin cluster. It therefore provides the same direct matched-window discrimination with the smallest sufficient modifier burden and least departure from the characterized reactive core.

residual_decision_risk: H-RESIN versus H-DUAL remains unresolved because both predict the same low drift for S1C41.
Uncontrolled process state and missing process fields may confound formulation effects with realization-state differences.
Modifier functionality and any required NCO:OH stoichiometry adjustment are not verified in the proposal.
The 7.61% falsification boundary is not robustly specified for repeat aggregation or uncertainty intervals, and the E1 reference is a single realization.
The small base margin to the first strictly lower experiment means the deterministic ranking provides limited separation despite its perturbation stability.
robustness_adjudication.skeptic_objection_reasoning: The strongest objection is valid: the dual-axis composition cannot distinguish H-RESIN from H-DUAL, and simultaneous changes in AC1920, TK100, and reactive-core fraction limit mechanism attribution. However, the proposed matched-window 120 C hold remains the most direct experiment for the established failure mode and can still distinguish the reactive-core linear-dilution prediction from strong suppression. The objection therefore limits the claims that may be made from its result rather than displacing this experiment for the immediate coarse suppression test. An acrylic-only hold, with verified modifier functionality, controlled preparation history, and prespecified repeat aggregation and uncertainty handling, is required as a follow-up for the acrylic-alone-versus-tackifier-required question.
robustness_adjudication.weight_sensitivity_assessment: The proposal is in the tied deterministic top set. No weight perturbation in the 25-scenario sweep changed the tied top set: top_experiment_set_stability is 1.0, and every recommendation_flip_boundary term survives the full 0.5-1.5 multiplier sweep. These perturbations are scientifically defensible because they vary decision relevance, hypothesis discrimination, uncertainty reduction, interpretability, extrapolation risk, and process-state risk over a broad range. The base margin to the first strictly lower experiment is only 0.004583, so the tie should not be interpreted as a large separation from alternatives.

skeptic.falsification_criterion_assessment: The protocol directly measures SI_15_60 at the required 15 and 60 minute endpoints, and the H-CORE-versus-H-RESIN separation for S1C41 is 3.804 percentage points, larger than the declared 2.00% resolution. Thus a result below 3.80% or at/above 7.61% can be produced by this protocol. However, the exact 7.61% boundary is not robustly adjudicable without defining repeat aggregation and uncertainty, because process state is uncontrolled and the E1 reference is a single realization.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: A low SI_15_60 result could support either resin-modification suppression or tackifier-required dual-axis specialization; it cannot support a claim that both axes are required or that acrylic addition alone is ineffective.
objections.objection: The dual-axis S1C41 composition (15% AC1920 and 5% TK100) produces identical registered predictions for H-RESIN and H-DUAL: 3.804% versus 3.804%. The experiment therefore has only two distinguishable outcome regimes, not three, and cannot test the stated question of whether acrylic-like addition alone is sufficient. The Proposer does admit this in "hypotheses_not_separated" and in the falsification criterion, but still labels all three hypotheses as addressed.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: The result may be interpreted as resin-specific or dual-axis rheological suppression when it could instead reflect altered reactive-group stoichiometry, modifier reactivity, or simple dilution.
objections.objection: The formulation changes AC1920, TK100, and the reactive-core mass fraction simultaneously. For S1C41, AC1920 is 15%, TK100 is 5%, and the reactive mass fraction is 0.8000. Thus a change in SI_15_60 cannot attribute suppression to the acrylic-like axis, the minor-tackifier-like axis, or an interaction between them. In addition, the local anchor explicitly warns that reactive OH or other NCO-reactive groups in modifiers require stoichiometry recalculation, but the proposal uses the 7.608% linear-dilution prediction without specifying verified modifier functionality or adjusted NCO:OH stoichiometry.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: An apparent drift difference could partly reflect preparation or realization-state differences rather than modifier effects, weakening the comparison with the single E1 reference trajectory.
objections.objection: SI_15_60 is directly measured from eta_15 and eta_60, so it does not inherit a model-fit or extrapolation assumption. However, the protocol does not control or match the realization state at 15 minutes: M-HOLD-120 has process_state_risk 0.75, controls_process_state is false, and six process fields are missing. Because the state-aware summary shows realization-specific viscosity displacement dominates the local variation, the proposal's matched-window comparison is direct but not necessarily formulation-specific.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: H-RESIN could be declared falsified at a boundary that is indistinguishable from ordinary measurement and preparation variation, or retained despite a result that is materially inconsistent with the linear prediction.
objections.objection: The H-RESIN falsification boundary is set exactly at the predicted linear-dilution value, 7.61% for S1C41, despite the declared 2.00% discrimination resolution and only two minimum repeats. The protocol does not define whether the threshold is applied to each repeat, the mean, or an uncertainty interval, and the 9.51% E1 reference used to derive 7.608% comes from one original run. A result near 7.61% therefore cannot robustly meet the claimed falsification decision even though the numerical criterion is operationally measurable.

skeptic.recommended_change: Add an acrylic-only 15% AC1920 hold with the same matched reactive-core fraction and independently verified modifier functionality, alongside the 15% AC1920 plus 5% TK100 condition. Use controlled preparation history and define the falsification statistic across repeats, preferably with a prespecified mean and uncertainty interval.
skeptic.strongest_objection: The dual-axis intervention cannot distinguish H-RESIN from H-DUAL, while simultaneously changing AC1920, TK100, and reactive-core fraction; therefore it cannot answer the claimed acrylic-alone-versus-tackifier-required question or support mechanism attribution beyond a coarse low-drift versus linear-dilution comparison.

claim_boundaries: The shared-shape/state-shift structure is established only within the measured local chemistry family.
The apparent E_eta descriptor is rheological, not a chemical reaction activation energy.
The E1/E5 hold contrast does not identify a unique molecular mechanism.
The phosphoric-acid-labelled E1 +P curve is not used in the chemistry-audited primary state model.
No validation-formulation identity or outcome is used by this tool.
design_rules: Represent a candidate as formulation plus process/realization state, not composition alone.

Use one state-specific anchor measurement to locate a new realization or nearby local formulation on the transferable thermal-response shape when it remains inside the supported local chemistry family.
Treat static viscosity, temperature response and thermal-hold stability as separate decision variables.
When the failure mode is hot-hold drift, choose an experiment and measurement window that directly test drift rather than only matching one nominal viscosity value.
Use external resin/tackifier evidence to define chemically plausible directions, but do not convert analogue proximity into a predicted local outcome.

one_point_state_calibration.interpretation: Within the tested local chemistry family, one state-specific viscosity anchor can locate a previously held-out nominal formulation on the shared thermal-response shape to roughly 6-10% pooled multiplicative error.
one_point_state_calibration.validation_scheme: leave one nominal formulation out; fit shared shape on the remaining formulations; use one anchor from the held formulation

state_shift_master_curve.interpretation: Within the chemistry-audited local family, a realization-specific viscosity-scale intercept plus a shared quadratic inverse-temperature response closes the data far better than a formulation-level intercept using the same thermal basis.

temporal_stability_coordinate.interpretation: Original E1 and E5 hold trajectories show that thermal-hold viscosity drift is strongly formulation dependent and should be treated separately from static viscosity.

thermal_coordinate.interpretation: The apparent temperature-sensitivity descriptor remains comparatively concentrated after chemistry auditing; it is a rheological descriptor, not a molecular reaction activation energy.

experiment_design_implications.hold_window: For the current local study, 120 C and the common 15-60 min window directly interrogate the observed instability while matching the available validation window.
experiment_design_implications.selection_target: Select a formulation-process point that is informative about the observed instability and state uncertainty, not merely the closest static-viscosity value.
experiment_design_implications.state_anchor: A single in-range anchor can be used for efficient local curve calibration; 120 C is operationally attractive because it is also the hold-stability test temperature.

provenance_audit.reason: The source record is phosphoric-acid-labelled and its additive identity/amount is not represented in formulations.csv; it is retained as sensitivity-only until chemistry is reconciled.

result.source_scope: original pre-validation local measurements with chemistry-comparability audit

The 15% grid level is retained as a lower-bound design point, but the literature denominator for the reported 15% addition level is not treated as an exact total-formulation anchor until reverified.

evidence: PAT_US5932680A: examples around 4.8-6.4% tackifying/hydrocarbon resin and preferred resin range 3-10 wt%
PAT_US20070155859A1: tackifiers/rheology-control agents typically used below about 10 wt%
minor_tackifier_like_modifier_pct_total.interpretation: 5% represents the repeatedly documented minor-resin region and 10% is a conservative coarse upper level.

result.claim_boundary: External examples are analogues. They support candidate-family and coarse-region hypotheses, not an exact optimum for AC1920/TK100 and not a proven local molecular mechanism. The current reconstruction uses only pre-result evidence at runtime; the exact validation coordinates and outcome are excluded from candidate construction, ranking and tie-breaking.

decision_policy.claim_boundary: This policy can recover an evidence-supported formulation neighborhood, but it is not a predictor of the exact wet-lab optimum.

acrylic_like.basis: 15% directional lower-region evidence plus directly commensurate ~19-20% examples; 25% remains directly supported but is a larger perturbation.

minor_tackifier_like.basis: Curated PUR examples repeatedly place tackifying/hydrocarbon resin near 5%, with broader guidance below about 10%.

experiment_intents.causal_isolation: Use when the primary objective is attribution of one formulation axis. Prefer a single active modifier axis only in this mode.
experiment_intents.performance_mitigation: Use when a measured failure mode is already established and the next experiment is intended to reduce that failure. Independently supported multi-modifier interventions are admissible.
experiment_intents.uncertainty_resolution: Use when missing process, stoichiometric or evidence information prevents an interpretable performance test.

decision_policy.purpose: Select an experimentally informative intervention from pre-result evidence without treating a literature composition as the hidden optimum.
ranking_rules: Exact distance to an external analogue anchor is audit metadata, not a primary optimization objective.
Candidates in the same evidence-support class are not rewarded merely for being numerically closer to a literature percentage.
For performance mitigation, two modifier axes may be combined when each is independently supported and the combination stays inside bounded evidence regions.

Among candidates with comparable evidence coverage and interpretability, prefer the smallest sufficient total modifier burden and the smallest justified departure from the characterized local chemistry.
A single-variable design is preferred only when causal attribution is the stated experiment intent; it is not a universal default.
Held-out validation coordinates and outcomes must never enter candidate construction, ranking or tie-breaking.

historical_status.interpretation: The prospective historical claim attaches to the Agent recommendation itself. The current coarse grid and fine-refinement software are later reproducible operationalizations of the evidence-constrained region and are not represented as the original contemporaneous freeze algorithm unless older provenance is recovered.

local_reactive_core_anchor.reason: E2 is the geometric centre of the original five-point local design: 50/50 PPG2000/PDP-70 and NCO:OH=1.80, centered between E1/E3 stoichiometric perturbations and E4/E5 composition perturbations.
local_reactive_core_anchor.stoichiometry_note: The E2 NCO:OH=1.80 label applies to the original reactive core. If a modifier contributes reactive OH or another NCO-reactive group, true stoichiometry must be recalculated from verified material specifications.

stability_hypotheses.H1_formulation_family: Partial replacement of the reactive-only formulation by an acrylic-like and/or minor tackifier-like resin can reduce hot-hold viscosity drift under matched process conditions.
stability_hypotheses.H2_functionality: At comparable acrylic loading, lower effective reactive-group density or lower-OH acrylic chemistry is expected to be more favorable for hot-hold viscosity stability than more highly reactive acrylic chemistry.
stability_hypotheses.H3_region: A useful candidate region is expected within the externally supported coarse space spanned by 15-25% acrylic-like modifier and 0-10% minor tackifier-like modifier, while preserving the relative E2 reactive-core proportions.

result.limitation: No thermal-hold curve and no direct match to AC1920/TK100.
result.pattern: polyoxypropylene diol + polyester diols + acrylic tackifying resin + MDI

result.agent_hint: Large viscosity changes across polyol-composition variants show that composition-level changes can strongly alter melt rheology; formulation-family changes are therefore reasonable when the observed failure is large.
result.limitation: Not a resin-modifier study and not a hold-stability experiment.

result.agent_hint: A peer-reviewed PUR study reported 15% acrylic resin as the overall preferred addition level in its system; this independently supports 15% as a coarse acrylic-axis candidate level.
result.limitation: Optimization target was overall high-temperature adhesive performance, not thermal-hold viscosity; chemistry differs from the local system.
result.pattern: polyether polyol + polyphenylene-ether polyol + acrylic resin + crystalline polyester polyol + MDI

result.agent_hint: A 25 wt% low-OH acrylic copolymer formulation showed substantially slower viscosity rise than the equal-loading higher-OH acrylic comparator; this supports both a 25% acrylic candidate level and the hypothesis that lower reactive-group density can improve hot-hold stability.
result.limitation: Different acrylic chemistry and much longer hold window; does not establish the local mechanism.
result.pattern: PPG1000 + PPG2000 + polyester polyol + low-OH acrylic copolymer + MDI

result.agent_hint: At the same 25 wt% acrylic loading, the higher-OH acrylic analogue exhibited roughly twice the reported 8 h viscosity increase of the low-OH example, making modifier functionality a plausible stability variable rather than loading alone.
result.limitation: Patent comparison; acrylic materials are not AC1920 and the result is not a direct local-system measurement.
result.pattern: same formulation as Example 10 but higher-OH acrylic copolymer

result.agent_hint: A functional-tackifier-containing formulation had lower reported stability rise than the no-acrylic/no-functional-tackifier comparator in the same example set, supporting the idea that modifier identity can change hot-melt stability.
result.limitation: Other formulation variables including MDI differ; not an isolated causal comparison.
result.pattern: PPG2025 + PPG4025 + polyester polyol + functional tackifier + MDI

result.agent_hint: The no-acrylic/no-functional-tackifier comparator reported a larger stability value than several modifier-containing examples, providing directional support for a modifier-family hypothesis rather than proof of one optimum.
result.limitation: MDI and other variables differ across the table; use only as directional evidence.
result.pattern: PPG2025 + PPG4025 + polyester polyol + MDI; no acrylic polymer or functional tackifier

result.agent_hint: The patent states that tackifiers and rheology-control agents may be used in small amounts, typically below about 10 wt%, supporting 10% as a conservative upper coarse level for the minor-tackifier axis.
result.limitation: No specific thermal-hold comparison and no exact match to TK100.
result.pattern: polyurethane hot melt with optional tackifiers/plasticizers/rheology-control agents

result.agent_hint: Published formulation art explicitly treats viscosity rise during prolonged hot holding as a design failure mode and cites a preferred stability level of no more than about 25% increase over 4-10 h; this supports thermal-hold stability as an independent design objective.
result.limitation: The time scale is much longer than the local 15-60 min test and should not be converted into a local numerical threshold.
result.pattern: thermally stable reactive hot melt urethane composition

voi_sent_to_model.formula: VOI = w_hyp * hypothesis_discrimination + w_unc * uncertainty_reduction + w_dec * decision_relevance + w_int * measurement_interpretability - w_ext * extrapolation_risk - w_proc * process_state_risk. Every component is normalized to [0, 1] by construction. This is a transparent normalized score with reported weight sensitivity, not a Bayesian posterior.
voi_sent_to_model.tie_note: These experiments share an identical component vector. The deterministic tool is indifferent among them. Any choice within this set must be justified scientifically.

top_cards.acceptance_criterion: Matched 15-60 min drift at 120 C stays below 3.80% across at least two repeats, i.e. below half the linear-dilution prediction of 7.61% implied by a reactive mass fraction of 0.8000. This accepts H-RESIN over H-CORE.
top_cards.falsification_criterion: H-RESIN is falsified if matched 15-60 min drift is at or above the linear-dilution prediction of 7.61%. H-CORE is falsified if drift falls below 3.80%, a separation larger than the 2.00% resolution threshold. This composition carries both axes, so it cannot separate H-RESIN from H-DUAL; an acrylic-only hold is the follow-up required for that.
